findings.message: sceneGrammar.ts's confusablePairs list (owned by task 2.1) omitted ค/ด even though it is one of the ten pairs task 2.4's own AC5 explicitly requires. Task 2.4 worked around the gap with a test-local UNDECLARED_PAIR_FEATURES dict rather than fixing the source list, so the two tasks disagreed about where the pair's distinguishing feature lives.
findings.recommendation: Declared the pair canonically (feature head-direction, matching the existing ค/ด mnemonic text already in symbols.ts) and removed the now-unneeded fallback in mnemonics.test.ts. Verified with sceneGrammar.test.ts, mnemonics.test.ts, tsc and biome.

findings.message: DECK_LESSON_IDS in lessonContent.ts still only held 'lesson-01' after task 2.5 authored, generated and committed four more schema-valid decks (lessons 02-05). Nothing routed a learner to them: /lesson/2 through /lesson/5 still resolved to the licensed video arm, so AC1 — 'every lesson in the opening band resolves to the deck arm' — was false in the shipped app despite the ledger recording it as [none]/waived with an honest gap note.
findings.effort_basis: lessons 02-05 already carry a stable legacyNumber/position in lessonSequence.ts, so the addition changes no lesson identity or ordering; verified by running the domain/script + presentation suites and npm run build, all green, plus fixing two phase-1 tests that had hardcoded lesson-02 as their generic 'still video' example.
findings.recommendation: Added lesson-02..05 to DECK_LESSON_IDS; added the positive AC1 assertion openingBand.test.ts had deliberately left unwritten; fixed lessonContent.test.ts and lesson01Deck.test.ts to derive a 'still on video' example instead of hardcoding lesson-02. lesson-sound-buckets is left undeclared — it has no legacyNumber to join the five-store identity hazard on, and assigning it a sequence position is a migration decision for the task that owns lessonSequence.ts's identity semantics, not something to decide in this round.

lessons.lesson: A ledger criterion marked [none]/[WAIVED] with an honest 'here's the gap' comment can still hide a real, fixable production bug — the gap here (DECK_LESSON_IDS not extended) was outside the authoring task's file-level `covers` but squarely inside the phase's folder-level covers, so it was fixable in review rather than a genuine planning blocker.
